covers_alert_paths: zzip/memdisk.c:195-210 -- zzip_mem_entry_new copies the local-header extra field with memcpy(mem, ptr2, ext2) where ext2 is read verbatim from the header's z_extras field with no check that the extras range fits within [buffer, endbuf)
povs.description: unzzipcat-mem against a ZIP whose local file header has valid PK\003\004 magic and z_extras = 0xFFFF, with the file truncated immediately after the filename. The magic check (33d6e9c) passes, the null check (64e745f) passes, and zzip_mem_entry_new's memcpy(mem, zzip_file_header_to_extras(header), 0xFFFF) reads far past the end of the file -- reproduced both before and after the official fix.
povs.exploit_path: unzzipcat-mem <zip> -> zzip_mem_disk_open -> zzip_mem_disk_load -> zzip_mem_entry_new -> header = zzip_disk_entry_to_file_header(disk, entry) (magic PK\003\004 valid, offset 0 in range, passes 33d6e9c) -> ext2 = zzip_file_header_get_extras(header) = 0xFFFF -> memcpy(mem, zzip_file_header_to_extras(header), 0xFFFF) reads past endbuf (memdisk.c:210)
povs.gap_summary: The official fix checks only the 4-byte local-header magic, not that the header's declared extras range fits the file -- a truncated header with a huge z_extras still over-reads the buffer.
povs.reason: oracle invalid at base 33d6e9c: this POV did not reproduce on the unpatched tree at the commit the patch is written for, so its outcome on the patched tree is not evidence about the patch

covers_alert_paths: zzip/memdisk.c:zzip_mem_entry_new -- after zzip_mem_entry_extra_block(item, ZZIP_EXTRA_zip64) returns a match, the block's z_usize/z_csize/z_offset/z_diskstart are read with ZZIP_GET64/ZZIP_GET32 with no datasize>=sizeof(zzip_extra_zip64) check
povs.description: unzzipcat-mem against a ZIP whose central-directory extra field is a 4-byte zip64 header (datatype 0x0001, datasize 0). zzip_mem_entry_extra_block matches the zip64 code and returns the 4-byte block, then zzip_mem_entry_new reads ZZIP_GET64(block->z_usize) -- 8 bytes at offset 4 of a 4-byte (post-fix) / 6-byte (pre-fix) heap allocation -- an out-of-bounds read that survives the official fix's walk bound.
povs.exploit_path: unzzipcat-mem <zip> -> zzip_mem_disk_open -> zzip_mem_disk_load -> zzip_mem_entry_new copies the 4-byte zip64 extra field into zz_ext[1] -> zzip_mem_entry_extra_block(item, ZZIP_EXTRA_zip64) returns the block (datatype 0x0001 matches) -> ZZIP_GET64(block->z_usize) reads 8 bytes at offset 4 of the 4-byte allocation -> heap OOB read (survives 03de3be, which only bounds the walk)
povs.gap_summary: The official fix bounds the extra-block walk but not the subsequent zip64 struct read -- a truncated zip64 block (datasize 0) still over-reads the allocation.

command_result.name: respov_opcode_base_zero_line_loop
command_result.stderr: [respov] reproduced: decode_line_info allocates without bound (ASan hard rss limit exhausted)

povs.description: nm -D -l against a crafted ELF object whose .debug_line header has opcode_base == 0 (line_range == 1, non-zero) makes every byte a 'special opcode' in decode_line_info()'s `while (!end_sequence)` loop, so DW_LNE_end_sequence is unreachable and the loop calls add_line_info()/bfd_alloc() on every iteration without bound. The pathological allocation is detected deterministically via ASan's hard_rss_limit_mb (the loop exhausts any resident-set bound), rather than via a raw timeout whose non-zero exit would be misread as 'blocked'.
povs.exploit_path: nm -D -l -> dwarf2.c:decode_line_info -> lh.opcode_base (attacker-controlled DWARF line-number-program header field) == 0 -> `op_code >= lh.opcode_base` always true -> `while (!end_sequence)` never terminates (add_line_info()/bfd_alloc() per iteration, no `line_ptr < line_end` bound)
povs.gap_summary: opcode_base == 0 makes the statement loop's DW_LNE_end_sequence path unreachable and allocates forever — the official fix's line_range==0 guard never runs, and upstream only added the `line_ptr < line_end` bound much later.

command_result.stderr: [respov] reproduced: NULL deref in xmlSnprintfElementContent (gap still open)

covers_alert_paths: xmlSnprintfElementContent has the identical unguarded c1/c2 dereference as xmlDumpElementContent, untouched by the official fix
povs.description: xmllint --debug --recover against the same crafted DTD (1.xml) as the ground-truth POV. --recover builds the malformed content tree carrying a NULL c1/c2, and --debug dumps every element decl through xmlCtxtDumpElemDecl, which hands that tree to xmlSnprintfElementContent -- the sibling function the official fix does not patch. --recover alone reaches only xmlDumpElementContent, the sink the fix does guard.
povs.exploit_path: xmllint --debug --recover -> recover-mode DTD element-content-decl parse builds a SEQ node with c2 == NULL -> xmlCtxtDumpElemDecl (debugXML.c:630) -> xmlSnprintfElementContent(buf, 5000, elem->content, 1) -> content->c2->type (no null check, unpatched by the official fix)
povs.gap_summary: The official fix null-checks c1/c2 only inside xmlDumpElementContent; the structurally identical xmlSnprintfElementContent is left completely unguarded.

covers_alert_paths: bitrate_idx derived from flags identically to samplerate_idx, but left unchecked by the official fix -- same missing-bounds-check pattern on a sibling field
povs.description: util/listmp3 against a hand-crafted 4-byte MP3 frame header (1.swf) with bitrate field = 1111 (15, invalid) and samplerate field = 00 (0, valid -- passes the new post-fix check) triggers a global-buffer-overflow read on mp1l1_bitrate_table under AddressSanitizer, both before and after the official fix.
povs.exploit_path: listmp3 -> printMP3Headers -> flags built from fgetc(f) reads -> bitrate_idx = (flags & MP3_BITRATE) >> MP3_BITRATE_SHIFT (4-bit field, range 0-15, unchecked) -> mp1l1_bitrate_table[bitrate_idx] (15-element array, valid indices 0-14)
povs.gap_summary: The official fix bounds-checks samplerate_idx but not bitrate_idx, which is derived and used the identical way -- a crafted invalid bitrate code still overflows the bitrate tables.

covers_alert_paths: TIFFGetFieldDefaulted(in, TIFFTAG_SAMPLESPERPIXEL, &spp): untrusted SamplesPerPixel tag read from the input file, no upper-bound check (tools/tiffcrop.c:5755)
if ((bps == 0) || (spp == 0)) return (-1): the only validation spp ever receives -- a zero check, never an upper bound (tools/tiffcrop.c:5932)

readSeparateTilesIntoBuffer: `for (s = 0; s < spp; s++)` read loop (tools/tiffcrop.c:992) iterates the caller's 8-slot srcbuffs[MAX_SAMPLES] pointer array with the raw spp=9, so s=8 reads srcbuffs[8] out of bounds and passes the garbage pointer to TIFFReadTile (tools/tiffcrop.c:994) -- a stack-buffer-overflow
povs.description: tiffcrop against a tiled PLANARCONFIG=separate TIFF (4_tile_9spp.tif: 64x16, tiled, BitsPerSample=8, SamplesPerPixel=9). loadImage reads spp=9 unchecked and dispatches the tiled separate-planar read to readSeparateTilesIntoBuffer, whose allocation loop is bounded at MAX_SAMPLES=8 but whose read loop `for (s = 0; s < spp; s++)` is not; s=8 indexes srcbuffs[8] past the 8-slot stack array (READ of size 8) and dereferences the garbage pointer via TIFFReadTile. This is the finder alert's PRIMARY sink. The benchmark fix (2f79856097f423eb33796a15fcf700d2ea41bf31) only bounds the combineSeparate* merge loops and never touches :992, so the crash reproduces both before and after official_fix.patch (upstream's real fix is the separate commit d9783e4a1476).
povs.exploit_path: tiffcrop in.tif out.tif -> loadImage -> TIFFGetFieldDefaulted(SAMPLESPERPIXEL)=9 (no upper bound) -> readSeparateTilesIntoBuffer -> `for (s = 0; s < spp; s++)` reads srcbuffs[8] past the MAX_SAMPLES-sized stack array -> TIFFReadTile on the garbage pointer -> stack-buffer-overflow
povs.gap_summary: official fix (2f798560) bounds only the combineSeparate* merge loops; the tiled readSeparateTilesIntoBuffer read loop at tiffcrop.c:992 still iterates `for (s = 0; s < spp; s++)` over the 8-slot srcbuffs[] array, so a tiled 9-samples-per-pixel image crashes both before and after the fix.

povs.description: tiffcp -p separate -s against a 1-bit, 1-sample, planar=contig TILED TIFF (1.tif) routes to cpContigTiles2SeparateStrips (readContigTilesIntoBuffer -> writeBufferToSeparateStrips, tools/tiffcp.c:1474). writeBufferToSeparateStrips computes rowsize = imagewidth * spp (1 byte per sample) and calls cpContigBufToSeparateBuf(obuf, buf + row*rowsize + s, nrows, imagewidth, 0, 0, spp, 1) with bytes_per_sample=1, cols=imagewidth, reading AND writing imagewidth bytes per row from/to buffers sized by TIFFRasterScanlineSize/TIFFStripSize (ceil(width/8) for BitsPerSample=1), producing a heap-buffer-overflow read and write under AddressSanitizer.
povs.exploit_path: tiffcp -p separate -s -> pickCopyFunc selects cpContigTiles2SeparateStrips (spp=1 avoids the only bitspersample guard) -> readContigTilesIntoBuffer fills buf sized ceil(width/8)*length -> writeBufferToSeparateStrips -> cpContigBufToSeparateBuf(obuf, buf+row*imagewidth+s, nrows, imagewidth, 0, 0, 1, 1) walks buf/obuf 8x past their real ends
povs.gap_summary: writeBufferToSeparateStrips (tiffcp.c:1474) copies imagewidth bytes per row with a hardcoded bytes_per_sample=1 into buffers sized for ceil(width/8) — the official fix never guards this tile->strip path.

[respov] reproduced: UBSan shift UB inside TIFFDefaultRefBlackWhite (gap still open)
tif_aux.c:159:19: runtime error: shift exponent 64 is too large for 64-bit type 'long int'

covers_alert_paths: td->td_bitspersample read from the TIFF directory with no upper-bound check -> 1L << td->td_bitspersample in TIFFDefaultRefBlackWhite's non-YCbCr branch (libtiff/tif_aux.c) -- the same shift UB, in a sibling function the official fix does not touch
povs.description: refbw: opens a write TIFF, sets BitsPerSample=64 with a non-YCbCr photometric (MINISBLACK), and calls TIFFGetFieldDefaulted(TIFFTAG_REFERENCEBLACKWHITE). The unset tag makes TIFFVGetFieldDefaulted compute the default, reaching TIFFDefaultRefBlackWhite's 'assume RGB' branch and its `(float)((1L<<td->td_bitspersample)-1L)` -- shifting 1L by 64 under -fsanitize=shift, both before and after the official fix.
povs.exploit_path: TIFFSetField(BitsPerSample=64, Photometric=MINISBLACK) -> TIFFGetFieldDefaulted(TIFFTAG_REFERENCEBLACKWHITE) -> TIFFVGetFieldDefaulted (tag unset, TIFFFieldSet false) -> TIFFDefaultRefBlackWhite(td) -> non-YCbCr branch -> (1L << td->td_bitspersample) at tif_aux.c shifts by 64
povs.gap_summary: The official fix guards the JPEG encoder's shift but not the identical `1L << bitspersample` in TIFFDefaultRefBlackWhite, still reachable via the public default-value API.

command_result.name: respov_ojpeg_readheaderinfo_zero_subsampling_fpe
command_result.stderr:
[respov] reproduced: UBSan division-by-zero (OJPEGReadHeaderInfo strile_length % (subsampling_ver*8), tif_ojpeg.c:1079)
OJPEGSetupDecode: Warning, Depreciated and troublesome old-style JPEG compression mode, please convert to new-style JPEG compression and notify vendor of writing software.
tif_ojpeg.c:1085:24: runtime error: division by zero

povs.description: A crafted OJPEG TIFF (Compression=6, Photometric=10 ITULAB, SamplesPerPixel=3, PlanarConfig=1, BitsPerSample=8,8,8, ImageWidth=16, ImageLength=32, RowsPerStrip=8, YCbCrSubsampling=(2,0), strip payload = 64 bytes of 0xAA). Read via the libtiff public API: TIFFOpen -> TIFFReadScanline(row 0) -> OJPEGPreDecode -> OJPEGSubsamplingCorrect (ITULAB+SPP=3 path calls OJPEGReadHeaderInfoSec, which bails on the garbage JPEG before the SOF component parse, so the tag's subsampling_ver=0 survives) -> OJPEGReadHeaderInfo: strile_length(8) < image_length(32) is true, so 'sp->strile_length % (sp->subsampling_ver*8)' = 8 % (0*8) = 8 % 0 traps (tif_ojpeg.c:1079). Built with -fsanitize=integer-divide-by-zero so the trap is observed as 'runtime error: division by zero'.
povs.exploit_path: crafted OJPEG TIFF, YCbCrSubsampling=(2,0), Photometric=ITULAB -> TIFFOpen/TIFFReadScanline -> OJPEGPreDecode (tif_ojpeg.c:670) -> OJPEGReadHeaderInfo (tif_ojpeg.c:674) -> 'sp->strile_length%(sp->subsampling_ver*8)' (tif_ojpeg.c:1079) divides by subsampling_ver*8 == 0
povs.gap_summary: The 2016 decoder_ok fix guards OJPEGDecode() only; the earlier OJPEGReadHeaderInfo divide 'strile_length % (subsampling_ver*8)' (tif_ojpeg.c:1079) still divides by zero when YCbCrSubsampling vertical factor is 0. Upstream fixed it only in 4.1.0 (43908ce15e8b).
